ordered_diagnoses: Multicystic Dysplastic Kidney with Ureteral Obstruction

facts.raw_span: A left perirenal fluid collection measuring 64 × 34 mm
Apgar scores of 8, 8, and 10 at 1, 5, and 10 minutes
serum creatinine was elevated at 156.1 µmol/L
mixed long and short T1 and T2 signals with internal light bands
A left perirenal fluid collection measuring 64 × 34 mm
Apgar scores of 8, 8, and 10 at 1, 5, and 10 minutes
serum creatinine was elevated at 156.1 µmol/L
mixed long and short T1 and T2 signals with internal light bands

concepts.why: Bilateral renal enlargement and hydronephrosis, along with a dilated fetal bladder and urinary retention, suggest congenital hydronephrosis.
The presence of a dilated fetal bladder, bladder wall irregularity, and bilateral ureteral dilation suggests posterior urethral valves.
The left perirenal fluid collection and elevated serum creatinine suggest renal dysplasia.
The combination of a dilated fetal bladder, oligohydramnios, and bilateral ureteral dilation suggests prune belly syndrome.
The presence of bilateral renal enlargement and hydronephrosis, along with urinary retention, suggests ureteropelvic junction obstruction.
The combination of a dilated fetal bladder, oligohydramnios, and bladder wall irregularity suggests megacystis-microcolon-intestinal hypoperistalsis syndrome.
The presence of bilateral renal enlargement and hydronephrosis, along with a left perirenal fluid collection, suggests autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease.

concepts.preferred_label: Multicystic Dysplastic Kidney with Ureteral Obstruction
concepts.why: The combination of a left perirenal fluid collection, bilateral renal enlargement, and hydronephrosis, along with urinary retention, suggests multicystic dysplastic kidney with ureteral obstruction.
The mixed long and short T1 and T2 signals with internal light bands in the left perirenal collection on postnatal MRI explain the urinary retention and bladder wall irregularity and thickening.

rationales.F03: Bilateral renal enlargement and hydronephrosis is a common finding in congenital hydronephrosis, posterior urethral valves, and other obstructive uropathies.
rationales.F04: A markedly dilated fetal bladder is a characteristic feature of posterior urethral valves and prune belly syndrome.
rationales.F05: A left perirenal fluid collection is suggestive of a renal cyst or dysplastic kidney.
rationales.F08: Elevated serum creatinine indicates impaired renal function, which can be seen in various renal disorders.
rationales.F09: The mixed signals on MRI are consistent with a complex renal cyst or dysplastic kidney.
rationales.F10: Bladder wall irregularity and thickening are characteristic features of posterior urethral valves and other obstructive uropathies.
rationales.F11: Bilateral ureteral dilation is a common finding in obstructive uropathies, such as congenital hydronephrosis and posterior urethral valves.
rationales.F12: Urinary retention is a common symptom of posterior urethral valves and other obstructive uropathies.
